heading.en: Make your own list of beauty

hook.en: If you had to list the most beautiful things you know, what would you include? Keats gives us his list, from the sun to old stories.

objectives.en: List the beautiful things that Keats mentions
Group them into nature and human imagination
Explain the image of the endless fountain

narration.en: If you had to list the most beautiful things you know, what would you include? Keats gives us his list, from the sun to old stories.

body.en: Keats names the sun and the moon, trees old and young that give shade to simple sheep, and daffodils with the green world they grow in. He adds clear streams that make a cool shelter in the hot season, and a thicket in the middle of a forest rich with musk-roses.

points.en: Trees, old and young, shading sheep
Clear rills (streams) and musk-roses in the forest

narration.en: Keats names the sun and the moon, trees old and young that give shade to simple sheep, and daffodils with the green world they grow in. He adds clear streams that make a cool shelter in the hot season, and a thicket in the middle of a forest rich with musk-roses.
Let us build a web of the beautiful things in the poem.

say.en: In the centre: things of beauty.
First the sun and the moon, shining on everyone.
Trees, old and young, give shade to simple sheep.
Daffodils bloom in the green world around them.
Clear streams make a cool covert in the hot season.
Musk-roses bloom in the middle of the forest.
Grand tales of the mighty dead, heard or read, are beautiful too.

body.en: Beauty is not only in nature. Keats includes the grandeur we imagine for the mighty dead and all the lovely tales we have heard or read. He ends with the image of an endless fountain of immortal drink pouring to us from heaven's brink: beauty is a gift from heaven.

points.en: Grandeur imagined for the mighty dead
Endless fountain of immortal drink: a divine gift

narration.en: Beauty is not only in nature. Keats includes the grandeur we imagine for the mighty dead and all the lovely tales we have heard or read. He ends with the image of an endless fountain of immortal drink pouring to us from heaven's brink: beauty is a gift from heaven.

heading.en: Sunny Trees Dance Round Many Tales

body.en: Remember the list in order: Sun and moon, Trees, Daffodils, Rills, Musk-roses, Tales. Say: Sunny Trees Dance Round Many Tales.

mnemonic.en: Sun - Trees - Daffodils - Rills - Musk-roses - Tales

narration.en: Remember the list in order: Sun and moon, Trees, Daffodils, Rills, Musk-roses, Tales. Say: Sunny Trees Dance Round Many Tales.

problem.en: Explain the image of the endless fountain of immortal drink.

steps.en: Explain endless: beauty never runs out.
Explain immortal drink: beauty gives lasting life and joy, like nectar.
Explain heaven's brink: beauty is a gift from the divine.

answer.en: It is a metaphor. Beauty is like an endless fountain of nectar pouring down from heaven: it never runs out, it refreshes and gives lasting joy, and it is a divine gift to human beings.

narration.en: Let us build a model answer together. Explain the image of the endless fountain of immortal drink.
Class quiz. Discuss with your neighbour, raise hands, and the monitor taps the class answer.
Now try CBSE board-pattern questions: assertion-reason and case-based. Read the passage carefully before you answer.

points.en: Nature's beauty: sun, moon, trees, daffodils, rills, musk-roses.
Human beauty: grand tales of the mighty dead.
Beauty is an endless fountain from heaven.
Both nature and imagination give lasting joy.

homework.en: Make your own list of five things of beauty and explain one.

narration.en: Recap. Nature's beauty: sun, moon, trees, daffodils, rills, musk-roses. Human beauty: grand tales of the mighty dead. Beauty is an endless fountain from heaven. Both nature and imagination give lasting joy.
